phase: 6 - FUA write, and what the follow-up power cycle does and does not prove

fua_write.kernel: mt6895-ufs-twoblock: zone write 608457 (FUA) ocs=0 polls=246 restored=1
fua_write.polls_ratio: 246 vs 39 -- the FUA command took six times as long to answer, which is what asking the device to commit looks like

what_was_attempted: reboot -p from Android (power off, not reboot)
the phone disappeared from USB entirely
no cable was touched by me; the operator reports the phone came up in fastboot on its own
what_this_proves: both blocks survive a power-off request and a subsequent boot
the FUA write put the same bytes on the medium that were asked for
what_this_does_not_prove: a real supply interruption. The operator says nothing was unplugged, and reboot -p on this board appears to land in fastboot rather than holding the rails down. Without a confirmed interruption the UFS device's volatile cache cannot be ruled out, so this is not evidence of power-loss durability -- it is evidence of surviving a reboot that was asked to be a power-off.
next: a power cycle with the supply confirmed gone: hold the power button to force off, or unplug the battery
a SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(10) path, since FUA covers only the one command
